people.name: Aga Khan III
people.summary: Led the Simla Deputation (1906) and was the first president of the Muslim League.
facts: Led the Simla Deputation of Muslims to Lord Minto (October 1906).
First president of the All India Muslim League.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Nawab Salimullah
people.summary: Nawab of Dacca who hosted the founding of the Muslim League (1906).
facts: The All India Muslim League was founded at his invitation at Dacca in December 1906.
Supported the partition of Bengal.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Aurobindo Ghosh
people.summary: Radical nationalist of Bengal; tried in the Alipore Bomb Case; later a spiritual teacher at Pondicherry.
facts: A leading Radical of the Swadeshi movement; edited Bande Mataram.
Acquitted in the Alipore Bomb Case (1908–09).
Withdrew to Pondicherry (1910) and founded an ashram.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Khudiram Bose
people.summary: Young revolutionary hanged at 18 after the Muzaffarpur bomb attack (1908).
facts: With Prafulla Chaki threw a bomb at a carriage at Muzaffarpur meant for the judge Kingsford (1908).
Hanged on 11 August 1908, aged 18.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Lala Lajpat Rai
people.summary: Radical leader of the Punjab; died after a police lathi-charge during the Simon protest (NCERT).
facts: One of the Radicals with Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal ("Lal-Bal-Pal").
Deported to Mandalay (1907).
Presided over the special Calcutta Congress (1920).
Died after the lathi-charge on the anti-Simon procession at Lahore (1928) (NCERT).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Bipin Chandra Pal
people.summary: Radical leader of Bengal ("Pal" of Lal-Bal-Pal) whose 1907 tour roused Andhra.
facts: A leading Radical of the Swadeshi movement.
His speeches at Rajahmundry and other Andhra towns (April 1907) started the Vandemataram movement in Andhra.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Chilakamarthi Lakshmi Narasimham
people.summary: Telugu poet whose verse "Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu" became a song of the Vandemataram movement.
facts: His poem compared India to a milch cow milked by the British.
Recited it at Bipin Chandra Pal's meeting at Rajahmundry (1907).
people.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

people.name: John Morley
people.summary: Secretary of State for India (1905–10); Morley–Minto Reforms.
facts: Gave his name, with Viceroy Minto, to the Indian Councils Act 1909.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Lala Har Dayal
people.summary: Founder of the Ghadar Party at San Francisco (1913).
facts: Founded the Ghadar Party among Indian immigrants in the USA (1913).
Its paper Ghadar was printed in Urdu, Punjabi and other languages.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Mohammad Ali Jinnah
people.summary: An ambassador of Hindu–Muslim unity until 1920; later the main spokesperson for Pakistan (NCERT).
facts: Played an important role in making the Lucknow Pact (1916) (NCERT).
Criticised the Rowlatt Act with Gandhi (NCERT).
Reorganised the Muslim League after 1934 and became the major spokesperson for Pakistan (NCERT).
Put forward the Fourteen Points (1929).
First Governor-General of Pakistan (1947–48).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

people.name: Edwin Montagu
people.summary: Secretary of State who announced responsible government as the goal (August 1917).
facts: August Declaration (20 August 1917): gradual development of self-governing institutions.
Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms → Government of India Act 1919.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Rajendra Prasad
people.summary: Joined Gandhi at Champaran (NCERT); later President of the Constituent Assembly and first President of India.
facts: Came into contact with Gandhi at Champaran (NCERT).
Congress president 1934, 1939 and 1947.
President of the Constituent Assembly; first President of India (1950–62).
Only President to serve two full terms (1950–62).
Bharat Ratna 1962.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

images.credit: Archives New Zealand from New Zealand / Wikimedia Commons

roles.title: President of India
roles.howGained: Elected by the Constituent Assembly (1950); elected 1952 and 1957

people.name: Bayya Narasimha Sarma
people.summary: Presided over the first Andhra Mahasabha at Bapatla (1913).
facts: President of the first Andhra Mahasabha (Bapatla, May 1913), which demanded a separate Andhra province.
people.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

people.name: Konda Venkatappayya
people.summary: Guntur leader of the Andhra movement; first president of the Andhra Provincial Congress Committee.
facts: A key organiser of the Andhra Mahasabha.
First president of the Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee (formed 1918).
people.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

people.name: General Dyer
people.summary: British officer who ordered the firing at Jallianwala Bagh on 13 April 1919 (NCERT).
facts: Ordered troops to fire on an unarmed crowd at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, on Baisakhi day (NCERT).
The Hunter Committee censured him; he was removed from command.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ali brothers (Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali)
people.summary: Leaders of the Khilafat agitation who wished to start a full Non-Cooperation Movement (NCERT).
facts: Led the Khilafat agitation (NCERT).
Mohammad Ali presided over the Kakinada Congress (1923).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

people.name: Motilal Nehru
people.summary: Lawyer who gave up his practice for Non-Cooperation; co-founded the Swaraj Party; wrote the Nehru Report (1928) (NCERT).
facts: Gave up his legal practice during Non-Cooperation (NCERT).
With C.R. Das argued for entering the councils (NCERT).
Chaired the committee that drafted the Nehru Report (1928).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

people.name: C.R. Das
people.summary: Lawyer from East Bengal, active in Non-Cooperation; co-founded the Swaraj Party (NCERT).
facts: A lawyer from East Bengal, especially active in the Non-Cooperation Movement (NCERT).
Founded the Swaraj Party with Motilal Nehru (1923).
Political guru of Subhas Chandra Bose.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

people.name: Bhagat Singh
people.summary: Revolutionary of the HSRA; threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly "to make the deaf hear"; executed at 23 (NCERT).
facts: Founded the HSRA with Azad, Sukhdev and others (1928) (NCERT).
With Azad and Rajguru killed Saunders on 17 December 1928 (NCERT).
With B.K. Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929 (NCERT).
Executed with Sukhdev and Rajguru on 23 March 1931, aged 23 (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

people.name: Chandra Shekhar Azad
people.summary: Revolutionary leader of the HRA/HSRA (NCERT).
facts: A founder of the HSRA (NCERT).
Took part in the Kakori train action (1925) and the killing of Saunders (1928).
Died fighting police at Alfred Park, Allahabad (1931).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

people.name: Sukhdev and Rajguru
people.summary: Revolutionaries of the HSRA executed with Bhagat Singh on 23 March 1931 (NCERT).
facts: Rajguru took part in the killing of Saunders (NCERT).
Both were executed with Bhagat Singh (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

people.name: Ram Prasad Bismil
people.summary: HRA revolutionary hanged for the Kakori train action; wrote "Sarfaroshi ki tamanna".
facts: Led the Kakori train robbery (9 August 1925).
Hanged in 1927 with Ashfaqulla Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Roll of honour KC Ghosh / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: B.R. Ambedkar
people.summary: Leader of the Dalit movement; led temple-entry movements (1927–35); later chief architect of the Constitution (NCERT).
facts: Born into a Mahar family; faced caste prejudice in school (NCERT).
In 1927 started a temple entry movement; led three between 1927 and 1935 (NCERT).
Signed the Poona Pact with Gandhi (1932).
Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution; first Law Minister of India.
Resigned as Law Minister in 1951 over the Hindu Code Bill.
Converted to Buddhism at Nagpur (14 October 1956); died 6 December 1956.
Founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha 1924, the journal Mooknayak (1920), the Independent Labour Party (ILP 1936) and the Scheduled Castes Federation (1942).
Burned the Manusmriti at Mahad (Manusmriti burning 1927).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 7 "Women, Caste and Reform"

people.name: Periyar E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker
people.summary: Founder of the Self Respect Movement (1925) in Tamil Nadu (NCERT).
facts: Had been an ascetic and studied Sanskrit scriptures; later joined the Congress, then left it (NCERT).
Founded the Self Respect Movement for the dignity of the lower castes (NCERT).
E.V. Ramaswami Naicker started the Self-Respect Movement (1925).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 7 "Women, Caste and Reform"

people.name: John Simon
people.summary: Head of the all-white Statutory Commission sent to India in 1928 (NCERT).
facts: Headed the commission that had no Indian member; met with "Simon Go Back" (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

people.name: Sarojini Naidu
people.summary: Poet and leader; first Indian woman president of the Congress (1925) (NCERT).
facts: Active in the national movement since the early 1920s (NCERT).
First Indian woman president of the INC (Kanpur, 1925) (NCERT).
Persuaded Gandhi to let women join the Salt Satyagraha (NCERT).
First woman Governor of an Indian state (United Provinces, 1947).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

images.credit: Bibliothèque nationale de France / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Pingali Venkayya
people.summary: Designed the Indian national flag; showed it to Gandhi at Bezawada (1921).
facts: Born at Bhatlapenumarru near Machilipatnam.
Presented a flag design to Gandhi at the Bezawada (Vijayawada) Congress meeting (1921).
Also studied geology and cotton ("Patti Venkayya").
people.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

people.name: Alluri Sitarama Raju
people.summary: Led the Rampa (Manyam) rebellion of the hill tribes against the British (1922–24).
facts: Led the Koya and other hill people of the Visakhapatnam and Godavari Agency against forest laws.
Raided police stations at Chintapalle, Krishnadevipeta and Rajavommangi (1922).
Was captured and shot at Koyyuru on 7 May 1924.
people.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

images.credit: The original uploader was Chavakiran at Telugu Wikipedia. / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Tanguturi Prakasam
people.summary: "Andhra Kesari" who bared his chest to police guns in the Simon boycott at Madras (1928); first Chief Minister of Andhra State (1953).
facts: Gave up a rich legal practice for Non-Cooperation.
Bared his chest before police guns during the Simon boycott at Madras (1928).
Chief Minister of Madras (1946–47) and first Chief Minister of Andhra State (1953).
Ran the newspaper Swarajya.
people.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

roles.title: Chief Minister of Andhra State
roles.howGained: First CM when Andhra State was formed (1 October 1953)

people.name: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
people.summary: "Andhra Ratna" who led the Chirala-Perala movement (1919–21).
facts: Led the people of Chirala and Perala to leave their town rather than pay the new municipal tax.
Founded the Rama Dandu volunteer corps.
people.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

images.credit: Andhra Desa Library Association / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Kanneganti Hanumanthu
people.summary: Leader of the Palnadu forest satyagraha, shot by police in 1922.
facts: Led the Palnadu peasants in refusing to pay grazing fees (forest satyagraha).
Was shot dead by police at Minchalapadu (February 1922).
people.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

people.name: Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary
people.summary: Led the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign (1921–22).
facts: Organised the refusal of land tax across Pedanandipadu firka (Guntur) during Non-Cooperation.
people.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

people.name: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan
people.summary: "Frontier Gandhi" who led the non-violent Khudai Khidmatgars of the North-West Frontier.
facts: Founded the Khudai Khidmatgars ("Red Shirts") (1929).
Led civil disobedience at Peshawar (1930).
First foreign recipient of the Bharat Ratna (1987).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Surya Sen
people.summary: "Masterda" who led the Chittagong Armoury Raid (April 1930).
facts: Led the raid on the Chittagong armoury (18 April 1930).
Hanged in 1934.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ramsay MacDonald
people.summary: British Prime Minister who announced the Communal Award (1932).
facts: Chaired the Round Table Conferences.
Announced the Communal Award (August 1932).

roles.title: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Jayaprakash Narayan
people.summary: Socialist leader; co-founder of the Congress Socialist Party (1934) and an underground hero of Quit India.
facts: Co-founded the Congress Socialist Party (1934).
Escaped from Hazaribagh jail (1942) and led the underground Quit India movement.
Led the Bihar movement and called for "Total Revolution" (Sampoorna Kranti) (1974) (NCERT).
Led a march to Parliament (1975) and the Ramlila rally of 25 June 1975 (NCERT).
Brought the Janata Party together (1977).
Bharat Ratna 1999.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Pattabhi Sitaramayya
people.summary: Andhra Congress leader and historian of the Congress; Gandhi's candidate at Tripuri (1939); INC president (1948).
facts: Founded the Andhra Bank (1923) at Machilipatnam.
Lost the Tripuri presidential election to Subhas Bose (1939); Gandhi called it "my defeat".
Wrote The History of the Indian National Congress.
Congress president at Jaipur (1948).
people.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

people.name: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao
people.summary: Founder of the Andhra Patrika; the Sri Bagh Pact was signed at his house (1937).
facts: Founded the Telugu daily Andhra Patrika (weekly 1908, daily 1914).
The Sri Bagh Pact (1937) was signed at his Madras residence, "Sri Bagh".
people.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

people.name: Kadapa Koti Reddy
people.summary: Rayalaseema leader who signed the Sri Bagh Pact (1937).
facts: Represented Rayalaseema in the Sri Bagh Pact (1937).
people.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

people.name: Stafford Cripps
people.summary: British minister who brought the Cripps proposals (1942) and was on the Cabinet Mission (1946).
facts: Offered Dominion Status after the war and a constituent assembly (March 1942).
Member of the Cabinet Mission (1946).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Vinoba Bhave
people.summary: First individual satyagrahi chosen by Gandhi (October 1940); later led the Bhoodan movement.
facts: Chosen by Gandhi as the first individual satyagrahi (1940); Nehru was second.
Started the Bhoodan (land gift) movement at Pochampally, Telangana (1951).
First land gift came from Vedre Ramachandra Reddy at Pochampally (18 April 1951).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Rash Behari Bose
people.summary: Revolutionary in Japan who founded the Indian Independence League and handed the INA to Subhas Bose (1943).
facts: Planned the bomb attack on Viceroy Hardinge (1912).
Formed the Indian Independence League in Japan; helped raise the INA (1942).
Handed over the INA to Subhas Bose in Singapore (1943).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Lakshmi Sahgal
people.summary: Commanded the Rani of Jhansi Regiment of the INA.
facts: Doctor from Madras who led the women's Rani of Jhansi Regiment.
Minister for women's affairs in the Provisional Government of Free India.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Aruna Asaf Ali
people.summary: Hoisted the Congress flag at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 9 August 1942 and led Quit India underground.
facts: Hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank after the leaders were arrested (9 August 1942).
Known as the "Grand Old Lady of the Independence Movement".
First woman Mayor of Delhi (1958).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Usha Mehta
people.summary: Ran the secret Congress Radio during Quit India (1942).
facts: Ran the underground Congress Radio from Bombay (1942).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Clement Attlee
people.summary: British Prime Minister who announced that Britain would leave India by June 1948 (February 1947).
facts: Labour Prime Minister (1945–51).
Sent the Cabinet Mission (1946).
Announced on 20 February 1947 that power would be transferred by June 1948.

roles.title: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Cyril Radcliffe
people.summary: Lawyer who drew the India–Pakistan border (the Radcliffe Line) in five weeks.
facts: Chaired the boundary commissions for Punjab and Bengal (1947).
Had never been to India before.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
people.summary: Scholar and Congress president (1940–46) who opposed the two-nation theory (NCERT).
facts: Born in Mecca to a Bengali father and an Arab mother (NCERT).
Believed in wahadat-i-deen, the oneness of all religions; opposed Jinnah's two-nation theory (NCERT).
Congress president 1940–46; led the Congress at the Simla Conference (1945).
First Education Minister of India.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"
